question.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, the exact solutions to the equation $3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}-{60}^{∘})+\frac{3}{2}=0,$ for $0\le x<{360}^{∘},$  are

${x}_{1}=$
 {{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}=$ 
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}-{60}^{∘})+\frac{3}{2} & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}-{60}^{∘}) & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}-{60}^{∘}) & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2}-{60}^{∘} & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2}-{60}^{∘} & ={240}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2} & ={120}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2} & ={240}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ \frac{3x}{2} & ={180}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2} & ={300}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ 3x & ={360}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘} & \, & \, & 3x & ={600}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘} \\ x & ={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={200}^{∘}+n\cdot {240}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain
$0\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={120}^{∘},$ and $x={200}^{∘}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

So, in ascending order, the solutions are

$$
{x}_{1}={120}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={200}^{∘}.
$$
